answer: Pin each agent to a verifiable network coordinate: a rotating quorum pings it at random, and the falcon-fast round-trip times triangulate its real location like buoys charting a reef. Two identities sharing one box collapse to the same point, so a jury flags the cluster. To make N sybils look like N distinct agents, an attacker must rent N geographically scattered vantage points and ride out every timing gale, paying real recurring hardware and bandwidth that scales linearly with the fakes, not a one-time fee.
